thread:
Liam O'Connor: FYI ACME just filed a ticket: after switching their SSO to Okta this morning some users can no longer download audit exports older than 90 days. They can list recent logs but export attempts for older ranges return a 403 with a weird retention message.
Evelyn Park: Can you paste the curl and response from them?
Liam O'Connor: Yep. From their engineer: 
```bash
curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGci...' \ 
  'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/audit/exports?org=acme-corp&start=2023-01-01&end=2023-06-01'
```
Response:
```json
{ "error": "forbidden", "message": "entitlement_retention_required: org_retention=365d required for export range requested" }
```
They also tried via Console -> Export and hit a modal error: "Export blocked: organization retention policy does not permit requested export range".
SRE Bot: Ticket #60214 attached by Zendesk Bot.
Zendesk Bot: Attachments: export-error-screenshot.png, okta-provisioning-log.txt
IdP Bot: Okta provisioning shows user mappings changed: users previously in group 'Compliance-Logs' now assigned to 'Compliance-Readers'. No SCIM 'entitlements' attribute present in patch.
```
PATCH /Users/jane.doe 2025-01-12T09:12:01Z groups:["Compliance-Readers","Employees"]
```
Evelyn Park: Hmm. The API error is specific to retention entitlement not present for the org or user. Two possible causes: 1) The org lost the org-level retention entitlement during migration (e.g., customer downgraded plan or provisioning lost the retention flag). 2) The user performing the export lacks a per-user export privilege even if org entitlement exists. Which does ACME claim?
Liam O'Connor: They say nothing changed on their billing side. Migration team mentioned they used a fresh SCIM import and mapped groups. I asked for one of the affected user's JWT introspection output.
Liam O'Connor: Introspect result they pasted: 
```json
{ "sub":"jane.doe@acme.com", "email":"jane.doe@acme.com", "scp":["openid","profile"], "roles":["employee"], "exp":1712345678 }
```
So no audit:read scope and roles don't include audit_view.
Evelyn Park: That explains per-user access, but the error message specifically mentions org_retention. We check our org metadata.
SRE Bot: Queried org metadata: acme-corp metadata shows "audit_retention_days": "90", "entitlements": ["audit_read"]
Evelyn Park: Org has audit_read entitlement but retention is 90 days. They're trying to export older logs (365d) so the export API blocks it regardless of user role. Where did the 365d come from? Did they previously have 365d and we lost it during provisioning?
Liam O'Connor: Customer insists they previously had 365d retention. Billing history shows they were on "Compliance Plus" until today; the migration process created a new org object (org id changed) during SSO consolidation and defaulted retention to 90d.
Security Bot: Any retention changes over 90d require manual Security approval per policy, so the provisioning pipeline intentionally defaults to 90 to avoid accidental over-retention.
Evelyn Park: Okay so two linked problems: 1) Their user tokens are missing audit scopes/roles (SCIM group->role mapping gap) so even if org retention is fixed they still may lack per-user ability. 2) Org retention value was reset to 90d by automated org creation during SSO consolidation, blocking exports beyond that window.
Liam O'Connor: Proposed remediation: immediate workaround = generate a one-off support-export for the requested range and provide the files to customer; medium = reassign org retention to 365d but requires Security approval; short-term fix for users = manual entitlement grants for specific users (audit_export_right) while IdP team fixes group->role mapping.
Evelyn Park: Customer is ok with us doing a support export but wants a durable fix. They also want an audit trail of who changed retention.
SRE Bot: I can run the export job as Support. Need explicit authorization from customer: request must be made by org owner email on file. Please confirm.
Liam O'Connor: Customer owner (alice.admin@acme.com) emailed approval at 09:40. She included the requested date range and said they need S3 transfer.
Evelyn Park: I'll kick off support export. Also logging change request: SEC-req-498 to raise retention to 365 for org acme-corp. Tagging @Priya for approval.
Security Bot: Approval required from Security lead for retention >90d. Audit trail note created. Need justification and org owner confirmation. Priority: high.
Liam O'Connor: Running export now. Command: 
```bash
./internal/tools/run_audit_export --org acme-corp --start 2023-01-01 --end 2023-06-01 --out s3://redwood-support-exports/acme/2023-01-06.tar.gz
```
Output: 
```
Export started (job_id=exp_9f3a). Staging... ok. Upload complete. Signed URL: https://s3.redwood/support/acme/2023-01-06.tar.gz?sig=...
```
Zendesk Bot: Uploaded file and added link to case #60214.
Evelyn Park: Customer verified download. Now for the durable fixes: Liam, can you coordinate with their IdP team to restore Compliance-Logs group or add entitlements attribute? Also request they avoid creating a new org during consolidation.
Liam O'Connor: I emailed their Okta admin and attached SCIM mapping guide. Requested they include entitlements or preserve original group names. Also recommended they add audit:read to the OIDC scope in their SSO app (so tokens include audit:read). They acknowledged.
Security Bot: For the org retention change I've created SEC-req-498 and notified Priya Rao (@Priya Rao) for approval. Include billing proof that they paid for Compliance Plus before migration.
Priya Rao: Approved after review. Changing org retention to 365 and logging the approval. Trace: trc_9b2e6d1
Evelyn Park: Infrastructure change applied: org acme-corp audit_retention_days updated to 365. Please validate exports and console behavior.
SRE Bot: Confirmed: Console export modal now allows ranges up to 365d; API export endpoint returns 202 for same request when performed with a scoped token.
Liam O'Connor: Follow-up for IdP: they need to either: 1) include scp audit:read in tokens (OIDC app scope) OR 2) make sure SCIM includes group names that map to audit_view role OR 3) include entitlements attribute in SCIM with ["audit_export_right","audit_read"] for org members. I sent examples.
Evelyn Park: Also creating a small alert: ENG-automation-741 to detect orgs created by consolidation with retention < historical baseline (e.g., if billing records show >90d previously). That way we catch accidental downgrades.
Liam O'Connor: Closing with customer. Notes to include in case: support export run (exp_9f3a), retention change trc_9b2e6d1, IdP coordination steps. Customer confirmed both export and console behavior OK.
Evelyn Park: Thanks. Post-incident follow-ups: - Update onboarding docs for SSO consolidation to warn about org creation and retention defaults. - Add a support-runbook entry for retention approvals and export request workflow. - Eng ticket for retention anomaly alert (ENG-automation-741).
